AttachmentMaterializationReason.description: Why Lash replaced an attachment with a model-visible placeholder.

oneOf.description: No provider in the shared adapter capability registry accepts this MIME/source pair.

AttachmentMaterializationSource.description: Stable source category carried by an attachment-materialization notice.

oneOf.description: Transient caller bytes.
Session-owned durable bytes.
Borrowed URL whose bytes Lash does not fetch.
Provider-owned file reference.

CellFailure.description: Structured failure returned by a code executor.

CellFailureKind.description: Why an executed code cell failed.

oneOf.description: The runtime refused the program because it violates a dialect or policy bound.
The authored program failed to compile or execute correctly.
Host infrastructure failed while preparing or executing the program.

EffectAddress.description: Canonical address of one admitted runtime effect.

ExecCodeFailureReason.description:
Why an `exec_code` effect failed before the executor produced a response.

This is the closed classification offline trace analysis keys on; the human detail lives in [`ExecCodeFailure::message`]. Serialized snake_case on the durable journal and trace surfaces.

oneOf.description: No code executor is installed on the session.
The executor's language runtime exited unexpectedly.
Any other session-layer failure; `message` carries the detail.
A journal entry written before the reason was typed: only the human message survived the erasure, so no closed reason can be recovered.

ExecutionNodeKind.description:
Closed vocabulary of executable workflow sites.

This describes the site, not its current observation. A workflow node may expose more than one site kind. Declaration order is the canonical order: a node's execution sites sort by it, so reordering the variants changes the serialized workflow graph and needs a graph schema bump.

ExecutionScope.description:
Stable semantic identity for one effectful runtime operation.

This is the scope admitted by the host boundary before nondeterministic work begins. Its journal encoding is an existing durable contract; effect addresses compose it with a replay key without changing those bytes.

GenerationOptionOutcome.description:
What became of one caller-requested generation option on one request.

Adapters emit what their wire can express and omit the rest — a model that pins sampling, extended thinking, or an endpoint with no seed field all take an option away without failing the call. This names which happened so a host can tell an honored request from a silently dropped one.

oneOf.description: The caller expressed no preference, so there was nothing to apply.
The caller asked for it and the request carries it.
A protocol suppressed the caller's non-empty stop list because its grammar owns the response boundary. This is intentional protocol ownership, but the caller's requested value did not reach the wire.

The caller asked for it and it is not expressible here: the endpoint has no field for it, or this adapter's use of the endpoint does not send one. Codex declines request controls by policy even when its underlying dialect has related fields.
The caller asked for it and sampling is pinned for this request, by the model's declared capability or by the thinking configuration in use.

The caller asked for an output-token cap above what this model can produce, and the request carries the model's capacity instead. The bound the caller asked for still holds; the number on the wire is smaller than the one they named.

GenerationReceipt.description:
Adapter-reported fate of a request's generation and prompt-cache intent.

This is request-side, adapter-owned bookkeeping and deliberately separate from [`ExecutionEvidence`], which carries only facts the provider reported about the execution. A host that needs repeatability asserts [`nothing_omitted`](Self::nothing_omitted) rather than trusting that a session-wide temperature survived every model it ran against.

cache.description: Fate of explicit prompt-cache breakpoints in the request.

GroupWakePolicy.description:
Wake rule recorded in a durable effect group's identity.

`Promise.all` and `Promise.allSettled` both use [`All`](Self::All): the caller's early exit on rejection is not a host wake rule. The wire shape has no default, so a missing rule cannot be replayed under a guess.

oneOf.description: Wake on the first settlement of any kind.
Wake on the first success, or after every child fails.
Deliver every settlement in durable rank order.
Provenance was not persisted by a legacy wire or durable payload.
Retry status was not persisted by a legacy wire or durable payload.

TraceAttemptUsageDisposition.description:
Why an attempt's provider-reported usage is present or absent.

Mirrors `lash_sansio::llm::types::AttemptUsageDisposition`, the vocabulary's owner, with the same wire spellings; the trace layer was the only one that flattened it to a free-form string.

# Integrator class

Reporting integrations exhaustively render these dispositions when explaining a call whose usage never arrived.

oneOf.description: The provider reported usage for this attempt.
The provider completed the attempt without reporting usage.
The attempt was aborted before usage could be collected.
The attempt failed before usage could be collected.

TraceChargeSafetyDecision.description:
Typed trace projection of one host charge-safety decision.

# Integrator class

Reporting integrations consume this optional component on an LLM retry attempt.

oneOf.description: Host policy permits this otherwise unsafe retry.

attempt_number.description: One-based unsafe retry number within the logical LLM call.

tokens_at_stake.description: Provider-reported tokens billed for the abandoned generation.

oneOf.description: Host policy refuses this otherwise unsafe retry.

attempt_number.description: One-based unsafe retry number within the logical LLM call.

reason.description: Typed policy bound that refused the retry.

tokens_at_stake.description: Provider-reported tokens billed for the abandoned generation.

TraceChargeSafetyDenialReason.description:
Why host charge-safety policy denied an otherwise transport-retryable generation.

# Integrator class

Reporting integrations exhaustively render these typed denial reasons.

oneOf.description: Host policy requires a provider idempotency or resume guarantee.
The per-call unsafe retry allowance is exhausted.
Provider-reported tokens exceed the host's duplicate-cost bound.
The provider's requested retry delay exceeds the host cap.

graph_node_id.description: Stable id of the span this record represents (e.g. `turn:<session>:<turn>`, `llm:<call_id>`, `tool:<call_id>`). Populated by the runtime for turn / llm / tool / session records so a consumer can build a nested span tree from `(graph_node_id, parent_graph_node_id)` with a single `id -> span` map. A language-execution record for a node event carries the observed node's structural id here, equal to the `WorkflowGraph` node id (ADR 0100 R0), so a host joins trace to graph on this key; a child start carries its parent node's id, and execution start and finish leave it unset.

parent_graph_node_id.description: Id of the enclosing span — the value of some other record's `graph_node_id`. A turn's parent is its causal origin (the spawning tool call / effect, via `caused_by`) when known, otherwise the session root.

TraceDurableTimerStatus.description: How a durable timer left its sleep.

oneOf.description: The timer elapsed.
The enclosing turn was cancelled while the timer was pending.
The session was revoked while the timer was pending.
The controller could not complete the sleep.

TraceDurableWaitResolution.description: How a durable wait left its park.

oneOf.description: The awaited event delivered a value.
The awaited event delivered a host-domain error value.
The wait reached its deadline.
The wait itself was cancelled.
A parked process command completed.
The enclosing turn was cancelled while the wait was parked.
The session was revoked while the wait was parked.
The controller could not complete the wait.

TraceEffectEnvelopeDiffEvent.description: Structural differences between the canonical envelopes on a failed durable replay validation. This event may contain prompt and tool-result values and must therefore only be emitted through the extended-trace gate.

TraceEffectEnvelopeDiffValue.description:
One side of a divergent canonical-envelope value.

Large values are omitted whole. Their exact serialized length and digest remain available, but no prefix is retained.

code.description: The failure code's spelling within its namespace — never the namespaced form. OTel `lash.error.code` projects this verbatim.

code_namespace.description: The namespace owning `code`'s spelling, when a code is present.

failure_kind.description: The transport's failure classification (`timeout`, `auth`, …), when the failure carried a known one. OTel `error.type` projects this — an absent or unrecognized kind projects `_OTHER`.

TraceExecutionEvidence.description: Provider-reported facts attached to one sealed LLM attempt.

TraceJournaledEffectStatus.description: Terminal status of a journaled `ctx.run` effect.

oneOf.description: The named occurrence has parked on an observed wait. Its `since` is the enclosing trace record timestamp, not a separately sampled clock.
A parked occurrence resolved, including cancellation. Its node terminal remains a separate fact.
Only an occurrence observed in flight may be cancelled.

TraceLanguageExecutionFailure.description: The observed cause of a failed language node.

oneOf.description: A dispatched tool effect failed with its recorded classification and recorded source and retry status. `replay_key` is the causing effect's identity.
A VM or host-boundary failure with a stable runtime error code.

TraceLanguageExecutionMap.description: The static graph of an execution, carried once on [`TraceLanguageExecutionPayload::ExecutionStarted`]. Identity (`module_ref`, `entry_kind`, `entry_ref`, `entry_name`) lives solely on the enclosing [`TraceLanguageExecutionIdentity`]; the map never restates it.

branch_memberships.description: Observed branch selections that admit this node's arm.

generation_disposition.description: Which of the caller's generation options the adapter put on the wire, as the runtime's `GenerationReceipt` serializes. Absent when the adapter does not report, which is not the same as reporting that nothing was requested.

request_model.description: The model identifier requested for the corresponding LLM call.

TraceProviderReplayKind.description: Opaque replay state rejected before an LLM Provider request was serialized. A missing minting route identifies a session written before provenance was introduced (or another unstamped producer); it is intentionally not inferred from the currently selected route.

body_json_omitted_reason.description: Why `body_json` is absent when the request body itself was observed.

body_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact serialized wire bytes. `body_json` is a parsed structured view whose re-serialization may not reproduce these bytes.

TraceRetryAttempt.description: One provider or tool retry attempt projected from the retry owner's sealed record. The trace does not own retry bookkeeping; it only renders it.

charge_safety.description: Typed host risk-appetite outcome when this attempt considered an otherwise unsafe duplicate generation.

generation_disposition.description: Which caller-requested generation options this attempt carried.

usage.description: Provider-reported usage for this attempt. Absence is not zero usage.

usage_disposition.description: Why `usage` is absent when it is. LLM attempts only; tool attempts carry none.

TraceRetryAttemptOutcome.description:
Terminal state of one provider or tool attempt in a trace retry ladder.

# Integrator class

Trace consumers exhaustively render these outcomes when explaining which attempt completed a call and why earlier attempts did not.

oneOf.description: The attempt completed successfully.
The attempt failed.
Protocol handling aborted after observing the provider response.
The attempt was interrupted before it could complete.
A tool attempt was cancelled.

block_id.description: The streamed block's own identity. Several blocks can share one `item_id` (OpenAI summary parts of one reasoning item), so block-level granularity needs this field.

TraceToolResultBlock.description: One ordered block of a traced tool result: text, or an attachment at the position the tool's value placed it.

TraceTurnCancellationEvidence.description:
Durable evidence that the traced turn was cancelled. Mirrors the runtime's `TurnCancellationEvidence`, which only [`TurnStop::Cancelled`] can carry, so a cancelled trace outcome can never be stated without saying which request produced it.

[`TurnStop::Cancelled`]: lash_sansio::session_model::TurnStop::Cancelled

origin.description: Opaque host-domain data. Lash records and returns it unchanged.

TraceTurnFailureReason.description: Why a [`TraceTurnOutcome::Failed`] turn stopped. Mirrors the non-cancelled `TurnStop` reasons.

TraceTurnOutcome.description:
The single terminal outcome of a traced turn.

One closed shape replaces the former `status` / `done_reason` / `agent_frame_switch` triple: each variant owns exactly the data its state can carry, so an agent-frame switch cannot be reported without a frame key and a cancellation cannot be reported without its evidence. Cancellation is its own variant rather than a failure reason — [`Self::is_failed`] is `false` for it.

oneOf.description: The turn reached a terminal result the caller asked for.
The turn ended by handing control to another agent frame.
The turn was cancelled. Not a failure.
The turn stopped short of a result.

WorkflowExecutionSite.description: Stable source-level location of one runtime site under a workflow node.

description: One durable trace record: the envelope fields plus the flattened event, whose `type` tag names the variant.

oneOf.description: One attachment was omitted so an otherwise valid session can continue.
Complete model-facing composition captured only when its fingerprint changes for a resident session.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the rendered system prompt plus ordered fingerprints of the model-facing tool contracts.

tool_schemas.description: Full model-facing tool contracts in request order. This is kept even when empty so the event is a self-contained snapshot.

error.description: Human-readable detail. Not a stable classification surface.

reason.description: Closed failure classification; offline analysis keys on this rather than matching `error` prose.

oneOf.description: A Restate `ctx.run` effect is about to cross its journal command boundary.
A Restate `ctx.run` effect returned its recorded or newly executed outcome.
A Restate durable wait has issued its park command.
A Restate durable wait resumed with a terminal resolution.
A Restate durable timer has been issued.
A Restate durable timer resumed or was cancelled.
The durable controller requested a quiescent handler-segment handover.
The runtime received a typed, non-retryable store integrity failure.
Compile/link evidence emitted before executing an RLM program step.
The program compiled and linked successfully.
Setup, parsing, or linking rejected the program before execution.

diagnostic.description: Bounded compiler or linker feedback, using the raw-error trace limit.

step_index.description: Protocol iteration of the submitted program within its turn.
